articles.title: Plans Approved for 23 New Homes in Kirkholt
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has approved plans for a new housing development in Kirkholt, which will include 23 apartments and five terraced houses aimed at providing affordable housing for local residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has approved plans for a new housing development on the Kirkholt estate, which will see the construction of 23 one-bedroom apartments and five four-bedroom terraced houses. The development will be located off Queen’s Drive and is being undertaken by Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), a not-for-profit Registered Provider that manages nearly 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire, and West Yorkshire.

The new homes will be available for social rent, priced at approximately 60 per cent of market rates. The initiative aims to address the local demand for affordable housing and is part of a broader strategy to regenerate the area. The site, which has been vacant since the demolition of an old block of flats in 2009, was previously used temporarily by Kirkholt Medical Practice before relocating to a permanent facility nearby.

Planning documents indicate that the development is intended to create a high-quality, sustainable environment that meets the housing needs of the local community. The proposal is also expected to help reduce anti-social behaviour associated with the disused site. MSV's vision includes creating a secure and outward-looking community that promotes tenure diversification.

In addition to the housing development, plans for a new community garden have also been approved. This garden will be managed by Q Gardens, a community group already active in the Kirkholt area, further enhancing the community's facilities and green spaces.

articles.title: Lift Out of Service at Derker Tram Stop Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Alternative step-free routes are available for travel towards and away from Manchester.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 16 August 2026, with no specified date for repairs. This disruption affects passengers using the tram service in both directions.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access is available via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street and must cross the tracks to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and encourages passengers to plan their journeys accordingly.

Passengers are advised to check the TfGM website for live travel alerts for further updates regarding the lift's repair timeline.
